overview: White develops the knight to c3. Strong players usually meet it with 3...Nf6 4.Nf3 (or 4.Bg5), reaching Classical or Stonewall set-ups, while the most played reply online is 3...d5, giving a Stonewall-style pawn wall after 4.e3 c6. White keeps a space edge and aims for kingside control of e5 and e4; Black builds the pawn wall and plays on the kingside, but has a bad c8 bishop.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nf3, Bg5 or Bd2, e3 and control e5, aiming for kingside play and the e-file.
Exploit Black's weak e6/e5 squares and bad c8 bishop.

black_ideas.idea: Build the Stonewall with ...d5, ...c6, ...Bd6 and ...O-O, then attack on the kingside.
Play ...Nf6, ...Be7 and ...O-O in Classical style and fight for e4.

typical_structures.structure: Stonewall: Black pawns on c6, d5, e6, f5 with an outpost on e4 and a poor c8 bishop.

character.notes: Dutch structures are unbalanced with kingside attacking chances and positional risks; unsure how sharp this exact branch is.

structure.notes: Stonewall pawn wall locks the centre; the Classical set-up is more flexible.

level.notes: Needs understanding of the Dutch structure and weak squares.
